metaDescription: Six torchiere floor lamps compared by lumens, color temperature range, dimming and shade type for uplighting a living room corner without glare.
expertTake: The SIBRILLE 72 inch torchiere is the pick for a bright, dimmable uplight with a wide color range. The Globe Electric 67134 is the value pick because it adds a separate reading arm. Skip torchieres in rooms with dark or very high ceilings, since the uplight needs a light surface to bounce from.
introParagraphs: A torchiere floor lamp points its light at the ceiling and lets the room glow from above. That indirect light is softer than a shaded table lamp and fills a corner without glare, which is why it has been a living room standard for decades.

Modern torchieres use LEDs instead of the old hot bulbs, so brightness, color temperature range and dimming are now the real differences. This guide compares those figures along with base stability, shade type and controls, so you can match a lamp to your ceiling and your evenings.

products.name: SIBRILLE 72 Inch LED Torchiere, 1800 Lumens, 3000K to 6500K
products.description:
The SIBRILLE is a tall LED torchiere with 30 watts of light and 1800 lumens, a color range from 3000K to 6500K and dimming from 10 to 100 percent. A large shade throws light up toward the ceiling, and the controls include both a remote and a button on the lamp.

The wide color range is useful, but the warmest setting is 3000K, which is softer than office white yet not as warm as 2700K. That matters for a living room used at night. Compared with the JOOFO at 3000 lumens, it is less bright but still strong, and compared with the Coucrek, it adds color tuning and remote control.

Place it in a corner with a ceiling of 8 to 9 feet, and leave at least 12 inches of space around the shade so heat can escape. Choose the warm end of the color range for evenings. For a living room that needs one uplight with control and range, it is the best all-round pick. A practical tip is to stand in the corner with the lamp on at night and look at the ceiling: a soft, even glow means the bounce is working, and a bright hot spot means you may want to turn the head or step down the output.
products.bestFor: Living rooms that need a tall, dimmable uplight with color control.
cons: Needs a light ceiling to bounce from
Large shade needs clear space around it

products.name: Globe Electric 67134 72 Inch Torchiere with Adjustable Reading Light
products.description:
Globe Electric packs two lights into one tidy lamp: a 72 inch torchiere on top and an adjustable reading arm lower on the pole, each with its own on and off switch. A three-way dimmer gives low, medium and high settings for the main light.

The two-light design is the strength and the sourcing issue. The main socket is an E26 type with a stated maximum wattage, and you should fit an LED bulb of the right size rather than the maximum wattage. The three-way steps are coarser than stepless dimming. Compared with the SIBRILLE, it lacks remote control and color tuning, and compared with the JOOFO, it trades remote control for a second light.

Check the socket label, choose an LED bulb with a suitable lumen output and use the reading arm for the page. For a corner where one lamp must handle ambient light and a reading spot, it is the most practical choice. Because the two switches are separate, you can leave the reading arm on at a low setting as a night light while the torchiere stays off, which is one of the quiet conveniences of this layout.
products.bestFor: Corners that need ambient uplight and a reading spot in one lamp.
pros: Torchiere plus a separate reading arm
Three-way dimmer for the main light
cons: Dimming is in steps, not smooth

products.name: JOOFO 69 Inch LED Torchiere, 3000 Lumens, Compact Remote
products.description:
JOOFO lists 3000 lumens from a 30 watt LED, the brightest output in the lineup, with stepless dimming and a small magnetic remote that sticks to the lamp. A built-in foot switch and a memory function that returns to the last setting round out the controls.

That much light can fill a mid-sized room from a corner, which is the strength, and also a risk: 3000 lumens is far brighter than most living room evenings need, so the dimmer is essential. Compared with the SIBRILLE at 1800 lumens, it has far more output, and compared with the mukuxin, it has a simpler design with a smaller remote.

Keep the remote in its magnetic spot or it will vanish, and use the lowest setting in the evening. For a larger room with a high or dark ceiling that needs more light, it is the best choice. If the room has a ceiling fan, check that the lamp head sits well below the blades, and avoid placing the lamp under a vent that can blow dust across the shade.
products.bestFor: Large rooms and dark ceilings that need lots of uplight.
pros: 3000 lumens is the highest output here
Memory function returns to the last setting
cons: Too bright in small rooms without dimming

products.name: GyroVu 70 Inch Torchiere with Frosted Glass Shade and Weighted Base
products.description:
GyroVu pairs a frosted glass shade with a heavy weighted base and includes A19 9 watt 3000K LED bulbs on a standard E26 socket. The glass diffuses the light softly, and a weighted base resists tipping.

Using standard bulbs is the main advantage: you can swap to a warmer or brighter bulb later. The glass shade is a classic look and a fragile part, and the light output depends on the bulb you use. Compared with the SIBRILLE, it is simpler and more serviceable, and compared with the Globe Electric, it has no separate reading light.

Handle the glass shade carefully and clean it with a soft cloth. A 3000K bulb is a warm white. For a bedroom or living room that wants a classic glass uplight that can be re-bulbed, it is a dependable choice. Frosted glass shows fingerprints during assembly, so wear clean gloves when you set the shade in place.
products.bestFor: Rooms that want a classic glass uplight with replaceable bulbs.
pros: Standard E26 socket allows bulb swaps

products.name: mukuxin 40W 4000 Lumen LED Torchiere, 2700K to 6500K
products.description:
The mukuxin lists 40 watts and 4000 lumens, a color range from 2700K to 6500K and dimming from 5 to 100 percent, with a high-transparency acrylic panel that reflects upward. It has the widest color range and the lowest dimming floor.

That range is the advantage: 2700K is the warmest evening setting in this lineup and the 5 percent dimming floor suits a movie night. The risk is the output: 4000 lumens is a large amount of light for most living rooms, and acrylic panels can discolor with long use. Compared with the JOOFO, it is brighter and warmer, and compared with the SIBRILLE, it covers a bigger color range.

Use the remote to set a warm, low evening scene and avoid placing the lamp close to curtains. For a big room or an open plan space that needs bright light with a warm option, it is the most powerful pick. For movie nights, set it near the bottom of its dimming range and bounce it off a side wall instead of the ceiling to keep the screen free of glare.
products.bestFor: Big rooms that want very bright light with a warm evening setting.
cons: Too bright for small rooms without dimming

products.name: Coucrek 70 Inch LED Torchiere with 8.7 Inch Round Base
products.description:
Coucrek builds a slim 70 inch LED torchiere on an 8.66 inch round metal base with a white resin plastic shade and a rotary switch on the lamp head. The listing says it works with smart devices through a rotary control, and it is aimed at corners in small spaces.

The slim base is the benefit and the tipping risk. An 8.7 inch base takes little floor but is the narrowest in the lineup, so keep it away from kids and pets. The plastic shade is light and cheap but less refined than glass. Compared with the GyroVu, it takes less space and uses a lighter shade, and compared with the SIBRILLE, it lacks a remote and a color range.

Place it in a corner against a wall, and consider a furniture strap if you have toddlers. For a small living room or bedroom where a slim uplight at a low price is the goal, it is the lowest-cost choice. In a home with toddlers, secure the base to the wall with a furniture strap, since a narrow base is the one that tips most easily.
pros: Lowest price tier in the lineup
cons: Narrow base needs care near kids and pets

buyingCriteria.explanation: A torchiere lights the whole room from above, so output matters. The Coucrek and SIBRILLE sit around 1800 lumens or less, the JOOFO reaches 3000 and the mukuxin 4000. For a small room, 1500 to 2000 lumens is plenty with dimming. Do not buy the brightest unless you have a large or dark room. A simple rule is about 20 lumens per square foot for general living room light, so a 150 square foot room needs around 3000 lumens in total, and that can come from this lamp plus one or two table lamps.

Torchieres bounce light off the ceiling, so they work best under 8 to 10 foot ceilings that are white or light. Dark ceilings absorb the light and tall ceilings dilute it. Check the ceiling before choosing the output.

Warm 2700K suits evenings, and the mukuxin offers it. The SIBRILLE starts at 3000K and the GyroVu uses a fixed 3000K bulb. Cool 5000K and up reads clinical at night. Pick a lamp that reaches a warm setting.

Stepless dimming, as on the JOOFO and mukuxin, is smoother than three-way steps on the Globe Electric. A remote helps because the lamp is often in a corner. A physical switch is a backup. Remember to test a remote from the far side of the room, because weak batteries and a lamp tucked into a corner can reduce range.
A tall, thin lamp can tip. The GyroVu has a heavy weighted base, and the Coucrek has an 8.7 inch round base. Place lamps away from walkways and kids.

Integrated LEDs cannot be replaced, so the lamp ends when the driver fails. The GyroVu uses a standard E26 bulb. Warranty length is a practical signal of durability. Warranty length is a useful tie-breaker between two lamps that look the same on paper.

howWeEvaluated.title: Light output
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared stated lumens, wattage and color range. The JOOFO and mukuxin led for output, and the SIBRILLE for balance. Brighter was not always better.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls
howWeEvaluated.description: Remote, rotary and foot switch designs were weighed. The SIBRILLE and JOOFO scored highest for control. Step dimmers scored lower.

howWeEvaluated.title: Stability and build
howWeEvaluated.description: Base size, weight and shade material were compared. The GyroVu weighted base scored well, and the Coucrek narrow base scored lower. Glass and acrylic shades were noted.

howWeEvaluated.title: Serviceability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at socket types and integrated LEDs. The GyroVu standard bulb scored highest. Integrated LED lamps scored lower for repair.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared each lamp with its siblings by price tier and features. The Coucrek is the lowest tier, and the SIBRILLE gives the best balance. Value depends on room size.

cards.label: Integrated LED
cards.text: The SIBRILLE, JOOFO, mukuxin and Coucrek have built-in LEDs. They offer controls but cannot be re-bulbed.

cards.label: Standard bulb
cards.text: The GyroVu and Globe Electric use E26 sockets. You can swap bulbs but have fewer built-in controls.

howToChoose.note: Choose integrated for control; choose standard for long-term serviceability.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Warm color, dimming and a base that stays put. Keep 12 inches between the shade and the ceiling.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The SIBRILLE is the best balance, the JOOFO is the brightest, and the Coucrek is the cheapest.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want control and range. The SIBRILLE and JOOFO offer remote and dimming.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You want a simple uplight. The Coucrek and GyroVu cover the basics.

maintenance.why: Dust dims the uplight and yellows plastic. A soft cloth keeps it clear.
Poles can loosen. Tightening prevents wobble.
Remote batteries drain. A fresh cell keeps control working.
Keep 12 inches between shade and ceiling. Heat can discolor surfaces.
LED bulbs drift in color. A new bulb restores brightness.

faq.q: How do I choose between a torchiere and an arc lamp?
faq.a: A torchiere lights the room from above with indirect light, while an arc lamp puts light over a seat. Choose a torchiere for ambient light. Choose an arc for reading. If you are torn, use the torchiere for the overall glow and add a table lamp near a reading chair.

faq.q: How much should I spend on a torchiere lamp?
faq.a: Simple lamps like the Coucrek sit at the lower tier, and bright remote-controlled lamps sit higher. Spend more for control and range. Prices change, so check current listings. Compare lumens, dimming range and warranty across two or three lamps rather than shopping on looks alone.

faq.q: How long does a torchiere last?
faq.a: The frame lasts years, while integrated LEDs and drivers wear first. Standard bulbs can be replaced. Warranty length is a good signal. Keep the vents of the lamp head free of dust and avoid draping anything over the shade.
LED torchieres run cool, but older high-wattage bulbs are hot. Keep fabric and curtains away and use the bulb the socket label allows. Choose lamps with a safety listing.

faq.q: How bright should a torchiere be?
faq.a: For a typical room, 1500 to 2000 lumens with dimming is enough. Larger rooms can use 3000 lumens. Choose a dimmable lamp.

faq.q: Do torchieres work with dark ceilings?
faq.a: They work poorly, since dark ceilings absorb light. Use a brighter lamp like the mukuxin or add other lamps. If your ceiling is dark, a lamp with a wall-washing head or a pair of lamps will work better than one very bright torchiere.
